name: Launch a new investment pool
summary: When the asset manager decides to pool an asset class, a cross-functional project designs the pool's strategy and guidelines, legal form and tax structure, valuation and unit pricing rules, drafts the trust and subscription documents with outside counsel, gets client and board approval, opens custody accounts, registers the trust for tax and configures every investment system. On launch day the clients' existing holdings move into the pool in kind at agreed values in exchange for units, which must reconcile for every client. It happens once or twice a year, so few staff have done it before; outside counsel, the custodian, client governance and board calendars set most of the pace, and private market pools add tax and commercial complexity.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian provincial public-sector asset manager with about $79 billion for four client institutions that moved from segregated client accounts to pools from 2020.
baseline.notes: Pools launched: Canadian public equities (November 2020), global and emerging markets public equities (early 2021), public market alternatives (2021) and infrastructure, the first private markets pool (October 2022).

trigger: The annual investment plan or a board decision calls for an asset class to be pooled and the pool project is opened.
end_state: The pool holds the transferred client assets, units are issued and reconciled for every client, pricing, transfer agency, accounting and tax processes have taken it over and the project is closed; or the project is deferred.

volume.seasonality: Launches were timed to month ends and to board calendars; none in 2019, one in 2020, three in 2021 and one in 2022.

evidence.note: Five pools launched from November 2020 to October 2022, about 0.2 a month in that window and 0.1 a month over the four-year period.

steps.name: Open the pool project and draft the charter
steps.description: The vice president of investment operations, as project lead, writes the charter for the new pool: asset class, clients and holdings in scope, target launch date, workstreams (legal, tax, accounting, pricing, custody, systems, client) and owners, and a status-reporting rhythm, using the checklist from the last launch.
inputs: investment plan or board direction to pool an asset class

error.defect_description: A workstream or dependency is left out of the plan.

evidence.note: Pool launches involved teams from all areas of the organization and detailed operational work on architecture, governance and legal frameworks. Times are author estimates for one pool launch; no published time study was found.

steps.name: Approve the charter, budget and steering committee
steps.description: The chief operating officer reviews the charter, confirms the budget for outside counsel and systems work, names the steering committee and agrees the target date with the CIO.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors in inputs pass through.

control.basis: Internal project governance: executive sponsor approves charter, budget and steering committee

evidence.note: Common project governance. Times are author estimates for one pool launch; no published time study was found.

steps.name: Define the pool's strategy, guidelines, benchmark and the holdings to move in
steps.description: The managing director for the asset class drafts the pool's investment policy statement: objective, benchmark, permitted investments, limits and the internal and external mandates it will hold, and lists which client holdings and mandates will move into the pool and which stay segregated.

error.defect_description: A restriction in one client's policy that the pool would breach is missed.

evidence.note: Each pool focuses on specific strategies and issues units for assets allocated from members' accounts. Times are author estimates for one pool launch; no published time study was found.

steps.name: Analyse the tax structure and transfer costs
steps.description: The tax manager compares legal forms (unit trust or limited partnership) for the clients' tax status, foreign withholding tax treaty access through a pool, and transfer taxes, stamp duties and re-registration costs of moving holdings in kind market by market, often with outside tax advisers.

error.defect_description: A market-specific transfer tax or treaty consequence is missed.

evidence.note: Private market pools need more planning because of tax and commercial complexity; pools could take years for tax and regulatory reasons. Times are author estimates for one pool launch; no published time study was found.

steps.name: Choose the legal form and instruct outside counsel
steps.description: Investment counsel agrees the legal form with tax and the asset class team, writes a term sheet for the trust declaration and subscription terms and instructs the outside law firm, setting the drafting timetable.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors in inputs pass through.

evidence.note: Each pool is governed by a pool document such as a declaration of trust or limited partnership agreement. Runs alongside the tax analysis. Times are author estimates for one pool launch; no published time study was found.

steps.name: Outside counsel drafts the pool documents
steps.description: The law firm drafts the declaration of trust, subscription agreement, risk disclosure statement and any offering memorandum, and returns marked drafts with open points for the model manager.

error.defect_description: A draft omits a required disclosure or misstates the unit terms.

evidence.note: External law firm drafting time is an author estimate.

steps.name: Review the drafts against the exemption order and client agreements
steps.description: Investment counsel reviews each draft against the securities exemption order (units only to members that are accredited investors; withdrawal terms, no misrepresentation remedy and a risk disclosure statement in the agreement), the clients' investment management agreements and the tax memo, and sends comments back to the law firm.

error.defect_description: A conflict with a client's IMA is not caught.

control.basis: Ontario Securities Commission decisions of 17 May 2017: prospectus and registration exemptions for the model manager pools apply only if units go to accredited investor members and the IMA or subscription agreement contains the required disclosures

evidence.note: Conditions are stated in the OSC decisions; number of drafting rounds is an author estimate.

steps.name: Write the valuation policy, unit classes and accounting rules
steps.description: The director of investment accounting writes the pool's valuation policy and pricing sources, unit classes, how income and expenses are allocated to unitholders, the year end and audit arrangements, and how client portfolios will account for units instead of the underlying holdings.

error.defect_description: An expense or income allocation rule is ambiguous.

evidence.note: Peer pools hold assets in trust, recover expenses through unit value and are audited. Times are author estimates for one pool launch; no published time study was found.

steps.name: Design unit pricing and transfer agency procedures
steps.description: The manager of unit pricing defines dealing days and cut-offs, the initial unit price, the custodian's net asset value deliverables and checks, the register layout for each client and the pricing error policy for the new pool.

error.defect_description: A cut-off or dealing rule conflicts with the pool documents.

evidence.note: Public market pools open daily and unit price is market value divided by units outstanding at a peer. Runs alongside the accounting policy. Times are author estimates for one pool launch; no published time study was found.

steps.name: Brief each client and collect legal and tax comments
steps.description: The relationship managers walk each client's staff, and often their lawyers and tax advisers, through the pool structure, documents, costs and the transfer plan, and collect comments and each client's internal approval steps.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors in inputs pass through.

evidence.note: Clients keep ownership of their assets and their own governance; consultation time is an author estimate.

steps.name: Steering committee reviews the document package
steps.description: The COO chairs the steering committee, which reviews the documents, policies, client comments, open risks and the timeline, and decides whether the package goes to the board.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors in inputs pass through.

control.basis: Internal project governance: steering committee approval before board submission

evidence.note: The global credit pool expected in 2021 had not launched by the end of 2022, showing launches can slip or be deferred. Shares are author estimates.

steps.name: Board approves the pool, its investment policy and documents
steps.description: The package goes to the next board or committee meeting, where directors approve establishing the pool, its investment policy statement, valuation policy and documents, sometimes asking for changes first.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors in inputs pass through.

control.basis: Board approval of new investment pools and their policies, with Finance and Audit Committee oversight of compliance in relation to the pools

evidence.note: The model manager's Finance and Audit Committee oversees compliance in relation to the pools; a peer's board approves pooled fund investment policies. Meeting wait is an author estimate.

steps.name: Prepare the custody account opening package for the pool
steps.description: Investment operations confirms the custodian still meets the qualification standard, completes the custodian's account forms for the pool and each market sub-account, gathers the trust declaration, signing authorities, tax forms and identifiers, and submits the package.

error.defect_description: A form, signature or tax document is missing.

control.basis: OSC decisions of 17 May 2017: custodians of the model manager and pool assets must meet NI 81-102 section 6.2 or 6.3 qualifications

evidence.note: Custodian qualification condition; custody account opening needs legal, structure and tax documents. Times are author estimates for one pool launch; no published time study was found.

steps.name: Custodian opens pool accounts, market sub-accounts and the NAV service
steps.description: The custodian runs its know-your-client and document checks, opens the pool's custody and cash accounts and local market sub-accounts, and sets up the fund accounting and net asset value service, chasing agent banks in markets that need local registration.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors in inputs pass through.

next.condition: more documents or market registrations needed

evidence.note: Files reviewed by two teams, paper documents and agent bank chasing make account opening slow; durations are author estimates.

steps.name: Register the pool trust with the tax authorities
steps.description: The tax manager files the trust account number application with a copy of the trust declaration, arranges foreign tax registrations and treaty forms the custodian needs, and sets up the pool's tax calendar.

error.defect_description: A foreign tax form is completed for the wrong entity type.

control.basis: Income Tax Act trust filing obligations: a trust account number (Form T3APP with a copy of the trust document) is needed for the pool's T3 returns

evidence.note: CRA guidance on trust account numbers; runs while the custodian opens accounts. Times are author estimates for one pool launch; no published time study was found.

steps.name: Wait for the trust account number and foreign tax registrations
steps.description: The Canada Revenue Agency issues the trust account number and foreign tax authorities or the custodian's agents confirm registrations; most of this wait overlaps with account opening.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors in inputs pass through.

evidence.note: No published processing time for mailed T3APP applications was found; overlaps with s14.

steps.name: Raise change requests to set the pool up in every system
steps.description: The director of investment applications raises and prioritises change requests to add the pool to the book of record, compliance engine, risk system, performance system, data warehouse, unitholder register and accounting interfaces.

error.defect_description: A downstream system is left off the change list.

evidence.note: Change management through IT change release per the organisation file. Times are author estimates for one pool launch; no published time study was found.

steps.name: Configure the pool in the investment systems
steps.description: Business systems analysts set up the pool portfolio, unit classes, look-through hierarchies from clients to pool, benchmark, data feeds from the custodian and reports, and test each change in a test environment.

error.defect_description: A hierarchy, feed mapping or benchmark is set up wrongly.

evidence.note: Organisation file: a software-as-a-service platform configured by internal analysts. Times are author estimates for one pool launch; no published time study was found.

steps.name: Code the pool's investment guidelines in the compliance engine
steps.description: A compliance analyst codes the pool's limits and permitted investments from the approved investment policy into the pre- and post-trade compliance rules and tests them against the holdings that will move in.

error.defect_description: A limit is coded with the wrong threshold.

evidence.note: Restriction coding as in the client onboarding workflow. Times are author estimates for one pool launch; no published time study was found.

steps.name: Run a mock valuation and unit issue with the custodian
steps.description: The unit pricing manager runs a dry run with the custodian: a test net asset value on test positions, an in-kind subscription and unit calculation in the register, accounting entries and the downstream feeds, and logs defects for fixing.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors in inputs pass through.

control.basis: SOC 1 control objectives over change management, new account set-up and net asset value processing require changes to be tested and approved before use

evidence.note: SOC 1 baseline objectives include new account set-up and change management; the model manager obtained a SOC 1 Type I report in 2021. Times are author estimates for one pool launch; no published time study was found.

steps.name: Prepare the in-kind transfer plan and launch calendar
steps.description: The project lead lists every holding each client will transfer, agrees the valuation point and prices for the transfer, plans foreign exchange, cash residuals and trades to align holdings, and sets the launch-day calendar with the custodian, external managers and clients.

error.defect_description: A holding or account is missing from the transfer list.

evidence.note: In-specie transfers reduce cost but carry operational risk and need many parties; the infrastructure pool needed an asset transition plan. Times are author estimates for one pool launch; no published time study was found.

steps.name: Send subscription agreements and transfer directions to clients
steps.description: Relationship managers send each client the final subscription agreement with its accredited investor certification and the transfer direction listing the holdings to move, and answer last questions.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors in inputs pass through.

control.basis: OSC decisions of 17 May 2017: units only to members that certify accredited investor status, with the required disclosures in the IMA or subscription agreement

evidence.note: Conditions stated in the decisions. Times are author estimates for one pool launch; no published time study was found.

steps.name: Clients approve and sign
steps.description: Each client's authorised signers, after their own staff review and any board or committee approval the client's governance requires, sign the subscription agreement and transfer direction and return them to the relationship manager.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors in inputs pass through.

evidence.note: Client governance timing is an author estimate.

steps.name: Go or no-go launch readiness review
steps.description: The steering committee checks every workstream's readiness: documents signed, accounts and tax numbers in place, systems tested, transfer plan agreed and clients informed, and either confirms the launch date or postpones it to fix open items.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors in inputs pass through.

control.basis: Internal project governance: go or no-go decision before launch

evidence.note: Common launch governance. Times are author estimates for one pool launch; no published time study was found.

steps.name: Custodian moves client holdings into the pool on launch date
steps.description: On the launch date, usually a month end, the custodian moves the listed securities and cash free of payment from each client's accounts to the pool's accounts and the transition trades settle.

error.defect_description: Some positions fail to move or move in the wrong quantity.

evidence.note: The Canadian equity pool launched with the transfer of $3.5 billion of assets; pools issue units for assets allocated from members' accounts. Timing is an author estimate.

steps.name: Reconcile transferred holdings and approve the opening unit price
steps.description: The unit pricing manager reconciles what arrived in the pool against each client's transfer list at the agreed values, approves the opening net asset value and initial unit price, and hands the in-kind subscriptions to transfer agency for the register entries.

error.defect_description: A transfer value error is accepted and units are mis-issued.

control.basis: SOC 1 control objectives: contributions processed and recorded accurately and positions reconciled to the custodian

evidence.note: Reconciliation and contribution control objectives; operational risk of in-specie transfers. Times are author estimates for one pool launch; no published time study was found.

steps.name: Resolve transfer breaks with the custodian and legacy managers
steps.description: The project lead works with the custodian and any external manager to move missing positions, correct quantities and agree cash residuals, then asks for the transfer to be re-reconciled.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors in inputs pass through.

evidence.note: Common in large in-kind transfers. Times are author estimates for one pool launch; no published time study was found.

steps.name: Approve the opening accounting for the pool and client portfolios
steps.description: The director of investment accounting approves the pool's opening balance sheet and the client portfolio entries that replace the transferred holdings with pool units at the agreed values, and confirms the pool is in the monthly close calendar.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors in inputs pass through.

control.basis: Pools' annual audited financial statements and the model manager's SOC 1 reporting to clients require accurate opening balances

evidence.note: SOC 1 assurance over controls supporting clients' financial reporting; audited pooled fund statements at a peer. Times are author estimates for one pool launch; no published time study was found.

steps.name: Confirm units and send final pool documents to clients
steps.description: Relationship managers send each client its unit confirmation, the executed pool documents and policies and a short note on how its monthly report will now show the pool.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors in inputs pass through.

evidence.note: Common practice. Times are author estimates for one pool launch; no published time study was found.

steps.name: Hand over to business as usual and close the project
steps.description: The project lead confirms the first daily prices, first month-end close and first client reports have run, hands open items to pricing, transfer agency, tax and accounting, records lessons learned for the next pool and closes the project.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors in inputs pass through.

evidence.note: The infrastructure pool's work became the blueprint for later private market pools. Times are author estimates for one pool launch; no published time study was found.

exceptions.name: Extra legal drafting rounds
exceptions.description: Open points with outside counsel, tax or clients send the documents back for another round.

exceptions.name: Project deferred
exceptions.description: The steering committee or board defers the pool, as happened to the global credit pool planned for 2021.

exceptions.name: Custodian needs more documents or market registrations
exceptions.description: The custodian or its agent banks ask for further documents, signatures or local registrations before opening accounts.

exceptions.name: Defects found in the mock run
exceptions.description: The dry run shows wrong hierarchies, feeds or unit calculations that must be fixed and retested.

exceptions.name: Launch postponed at go or no-go
exceptions.description: Open items at the readiness review move the launch to a later month end.

exceptions.name: Transfer breaks
exceptions.description: Some holdings do not arrive or arrive in the wrong quantity and are corrected with the custodian before units are confirmed.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from project start to project close

evidence.note: Public market pool architecture work ran through 2020 before the November 2020 launch; infrastructure pool work began in 2021 and its first phase launched in October 2022; the global credit pool expected in 2021 had not launched by the end of 2022. Durations are derived from these dates, not stated.
Canadian, global and emerging markets equities, public market alternatives and infrastructure.

benchmarks.population: The model manager Canadian Public Equities Pool, November 2020

pain_points.description: Private market pools need legal structures and asset transition plans that respect partnership agreements, co-investors and tax, so they launch in phases over years rather than months.
Custody account and market sub-account opening is paper-based and sequential, with documents checked by several teams and agent banks chased by email.
In-kind transfers save trading costs but involve many parties and carry operational risk; breaks must be cleared before units are confirmed for every client.
Launches are rare, so knowledge sits in a checklist and a few people; system set-up and testing across many platforms is redone for each pool.

evidence.note: Author estimate; once or twice a year per the organisation file.

pain_points.description: Board meetings and each client's own governance set the pace of approvals and signatures.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

sources.title: The model manager 2020 Annual Report
sources.supports: Canadian Public Equities Pool launched November 2020 with transfer of about $3.5 billion; detailed operational work on the architecture, governance and legal frameworks of public market pools; global and emerging markets equity pools established early 2021; private market pools could take several years for commercial, tax and regulatory reasons. Read from a text copy saved under scratch/ by earlier work.

sources.title: The model manager 2021 Annual Report
sources.supports: Enhanced quarterly risk reports for clients and the Board and a new Quarterly Risk Insights report in 2021; risk measured with sensitivities, historical and custom stress tests, total, active and factor risk and a liquidity coverage ratio; new risk and total portfolio management system selected in 2021 for delivery in 2022; investment risk support facilitates transaction reviews; private market risks assessed by a devoted team; Management Investment Committee co-chaired by the CIO and CRO and Investment Department Committees co-chaired by Investments and Investment Risk; three pools launched in 2021 and work begun on private equity and infrastructure pools; pooling brings efficiencies in pool activities and cash management; clean SOC 1 Type I report as at 30 September 2021. Read from a text copy saved under scratch/ by earlier work.

sources.title: The model manager 2022 Annual Report
sources.supports: More stress tests and scenario analysis in 2022 (historical, prospective single and combined shocks, inflation and rate scenarios); investment risk support facilitates transaction reviews and limit monitoring; Infrastructure Pool, the first private markets pool ($8.4 billion), needed legal structures and an asset transition plan, launched first phase October 2022 then transferred client holdings; new risk system partly live December 2022. Read from a text copy saved under scratch/ by earlier work.

Read from a text copy saved under scratch/ by earlier work.

sources.title: T3 Trust Guide (T4013)
sources.supports: A trustee applies for a trust account number with Form T3APP (or online registration) and sends a copy of the trust document; unit trust definitions.

sources.title: Pooled Funds (BCI web page)
sources.supports: A peer public-sector manager holds all pooled assets in trust with clients holding units; its board approves pooled fund investment policies; public market pools open daily and private market pools typically annually; unit price is market value divided by units outstanding; pooled funds are audited and a SOC 1 audit is performed.

sources.title: Transforming custody account opening with technology (roundtable)
sources.supports: Custody account opening needs legal agreements, structure documents, tax forms and regulatory disclosures, some notarised or hand-signed; files reviewed by at least two people in separate teams; sequential, paper-based processing, re-keying and chasing of agent banks cause long timelines.

sources.title: Client case study: Managing transition costs when consolidating pension funds
sources.supports: In-specie transfers instead of liquidation can materially reduce costs but carry operational risk; 17 parties coordinated with weekly project calls; a hybrid of in-specie transfers, cash redemptions, subscriptions and unit re-registrations. Read from a text copy saved under scratch/ by earlier work.

sources.supports: Toronto hourly wages for NOC 10010: low 41.21, median 62.37, high 96.15 (reference period 2023-2024).

assumptions: One case is one pool from project start to project close. Later transfers of further holdings into an existing pool (such as the infrastructure pool's second phase) are treated as part of the launch.

The in-kind subscriptions on launch day are entered in the unitholder register by the pool unit transactions process (its in-kind path), which lists pool launches as a trigger; this workflow reconciles the transfer and approves the opening price and accounting.

Several steps run in parallel in practice (tax analysis and legal instructions; accounting and pricing design; account opening, tax registration and system set-up). They are listed in sequence with short waits and concurrent_with references, so the simulated elapsed time follows the longest chain.

The asset class lead is shown as the managing director of public equities because four of the five pools in the period were public market pools; for the infrastructure pool the managing director of infrastructure played this part.
The board is an external party in the organisation file, so its approval step uses role external with no hands-on time; preparing the board paper is inside the steering committee step.
Business systems analysts and a compliance analyst take part although the process map does not list them; both roles exist in the organisation file.

Loaded costs come from the organisation file. Staffing: about 0.5 FTE stated across eleven roles averaged over a year with roughly 1.4 launches; hands-on time times volume implies about 0.7 FTE, reflecting peaks of work around each launch.
Times, waits and branch probabilities are author estimates (tier C); the overall duration is calibrated to the launch dates in the model manager's annual reports.
